column1: # id|reference(s)|category|difficulty|stem|correct;distractor;distractor;distractor|explanation

joram-arrow|2 Kings 9:21-26|Royal deaths|advanced|Who shot Joram, son of Ahab and king of Israel, through the heart near Jezreel?|Jehu;Hazael;Pekah;Zimri|Jehu drew his bow and struck Joram. This is Joram of Israel, not the similarly named king of Judah; the other rulers are not the archer in this scene.

jezebel-agents|2 Kings 9:32-33|Royal deaths|advanced|At Jehu's command, who physically threw Jezebel down from the window?|The eunuchs who looked out;The elders of Samaria;The sons of the prophets;The captains guarding the gate|Jehu gave the command; the eunuchs at the window carried it out. The account distinguishes the commanding king from the people who threw her down.

ahab-wound|1 Kings 22:30-35|Wars and battles|advanced|How does 1 Kings describe the person whose arrow wounded the disguised Ahab at Ramoth-gilead?|An unnamed man who drew his bow;The king of Syria leading his chariots;Jehoshaphat commanding Judah's forces;Micaiah accompanying Israel's army|The narrative identifies the archer only as a man who drew his bow at a venture. It does not name him or identify him as one of the other figures.

saul-narrator|1 Samuel 31:3-5|Royal deaths|intermediate|According to the narrator in 1 Samuel 31, what did Saul do when his armour-bearer refused to kill him?|Fell on his own sword;Surrendered to the Philistines;Escaped to Jabesh-gilead;Ordered Jonathan to kill him|The narrator says Saul took his sword and fell on it. The armour-bearer refused the request, and a later report in 2 Samuel must not replace this account.

saul-claim|2 Samuel 1:6-10|Textual nuance|advanced|In his report to David, what did the Amalekite claim he had done for the wounded Saul?|Killed Saul at Saul's request;Carried Saul away from battle;Hidden Saul's crown from the enemy;Buried Saul with his sons|These are the Amalekite's reported words: he claimed to have killed Saul. This question concerns his testimony, rather than asserting that the narrator independently confirms it.

amon-aftermath|2 Kings 21:23-26|Kings and succession|advanced|After Amon's servants killed him, who killed the conspirators and made Josiah king?|The people of the land;The king of Assyria;The servants of Pharaoh;The captains of Babylon|The passage assigns both the retaliation and Josiah's installation to the people of the land, not to a foreign power.

abimelech-final|Judges 9:52-54|Royal deaths|advanced|After a woman fractured Abimelech's skull with a millstone at Thebez, who delivered the sword thrust at his request?|His armour-bearer;His brother Jotham;His rival Gaal;His officer Zebul|The woman caused the head injury; Abimelech then asked his armour-bearer to kill him. The question separates the wound from the final sword thrust.

abimelech-place|Judges 9:50-54|Geography|advanced|At which town did a woman drop the millstone that struck Abimelech?|Thebez;Shechem;Ophrah;Succoth|The tower episode is set at Thebez. Shechem belongs to the preceding campaign, so the two places must not be combined.

agag-agent|1 Samuel 15:32-33|Royal deaths|intermediate|Who personally put Agag to death at Gilgal after Saul had spared him?|Samuel;Saul;Jonathan;Abner|Samuel called for Agag and carried out the execution before Jehovah at Gilgal; Saul's earlier sparing of him is a different action.

nob-agent|1 Samuel 22:17-20|Royal deaths|advanced|When Saul's servants refused to strike the priests at Nob, who carried out Saul's command?|Doeg the Edomite;Abner son of Ner;Jonathan son of Saul;Ahimelech son of Ahitub|Saul issued the order, but Doeg turned and struck the priests. Ahimelech was among the accused priests, not the executioner.

abner-agent|2 Samuel 3:27-30|Royal deaths|intermediate|Who took Abner aside at the gate of Hebron and struck him in revenge for Asahel?|Joab;David;Ish-bosheth;Benaiah|Joab took Abner aside and struck him. David explicitly disclaimed responsibility for Abner's blood.

ishbosheth-assassins|2 Samuel 4:5-7|Royal deaths|advanced|Which two sons of Rimmon entered Ish-bosheth's house and killed him?|Rechab and Baanah;Joab and Abishai;Hophni and Phinehas;Nadab and Abihu|The narrative names Rechab and Baanah as the pair who entered his house and struck him. The other named pairs belong to different households and episodes.

uriah-order|2 Samuel 11:14-17|Wars and battles|advanced|Who wrote the letter instructing Joab to place Uriah in the fiercest fighting and withdraw from him?|David;Absalom;Ahithophel;Abner|David wrote the instructions and sent them by Uriah. Joab implemented the military arrangement; this is not an account of David personally striking Uriah.

amnon-order|2 Samuel 13:28-29|Royal deaths|advanced|Who ordered his servants to kill Amnon when his heart was merry with wine?|Absalom;David;Jonadab;Joab|Absalom gave the order and his servants did as commanded. The passage distinguishes the instigator from the servants who acted.

adonijah-execution|1 Kings 2:23-25|Royal deaths|advanced|Whom did Solomon send to execute Adonijah after the request concerning Abishag?|Benaiah son of Jehoiada;Joab son of Zeruiah;Shimei son of Gera;Zadok the priest|Solomon sent Benaiah, who struck Adonijah. The king's order and Benaiah's action are separate roles.

zimri-fire|1 Kings 16:18-19|Royal deaths|advanced|When he saw that Tirzah had been taken, what did Zimri do?|Burned the king's house over himself;Fled to the king of Egypt;Surrendered to Tibni;Escaped across the Jordan|Zimri entered the palace and burned the king's house over himself. This is the narrated end of his brief reign, not an escape or surrender.

nadab-siege|1 Kings 15:27-28|Wars and battles|advanced|At which Philistine town under siege did Baasha kill Nadab son of Jeroboam?|Gibbethon;Gath;Ekron;Ashdod|Nadab and Israel were besieging Gibbethon when Baasha conspired against and struck him. The other options are Philistine towns, but not this siege location.

elah-assassin|1 Kings 16:8-10|Kings and succession|advanced|Which chariot commander killed Elah while the king was drinking in Arza's house at Tirzah?|Zimri;Omri;Tibni;Baasha|Zimri commanded half the chariots and killed Elah. Omri and Tibni figure in the subsequent struggle, while Baasha was Elah's father.

ahaziah-israel|1 Kings 22:51;2 Kings 1:2-4|Same-name identities|advanced|Which king sent to consult Baal-zebub of Ekron after falling through a lattice in Samaria?|Ahaziah son of Ahab;Ahaziah son of Jehoram;Joash son of Ahaziah;Amaziah son of Joash|This is Ahaziah of Israel, the son of Ahab. Ahaziah of Judah and his successors belong to a different royal line.

azariah-joash|2 Chronicles 24:20-22|Same-name identities|mastery|Which Zechariah was stoned in the temple court at King Joash's command?|Zechariah son of Jehoiada;Zechariah son of Berechiah;Zechariah son of Jeroboam;Zechariah father of John|The passage identifies the speaker as Jehoiada's son and recalls his father's kindness to Joash. The other Zechariahs have different fathers and narrative settings.

amaziah-death|2 Kings 14:19-20|Geography|advanced|To which city did Amaziah flee before conspirators killed him there?|Lachish;Jerusalem;Hebron;Libnah|He fled from Jerusalem to Lachish; his body was subsequently brought back for burial. The place of death must not be confused with the burial city.

josiah-chronicles|2 Chronicles 35:23-24|Textual nuance|mastery|In Chronicles' account, where did Josiah die after being wounded by archers at Megiddo?|Jerusalem;Megiddo;Riblah;Lachish|Chronicles says his servants brought him to Jerusalem and he died. The question explicitly asks about this account and distinguishes the wound site from the subsequent location.

gedaliah-assassin|2 Kings 25:22-25|Kings and succession|advanced|Who led the party that killed Gedaliah son of Ahikam at Mizpah?|Ishmael son of Nethaniah;Johanan son of Kareah;Seraiah son of Tanhumeth;Jaazaniah son of the Maacathite|Ishmael came with ten men and struck Gedaliah. The other names appear among leaders in the surrounding passage, but are not identified as leading this assassination.

zedekiah-sequence|2 Kings 25:6-7|Exile and restoration|advanced|Which sequence is recorded for Zedekiah at Riblah?|His sons were killed, then he was blinded;He was blinded, then his sons were killed;He was released, then made governor;He was crowned, then sent to Egypt|The king saw his sons killed before his eyes were put out. The passage then describes his binding and transport to Babylon, not his execution at Riblah.

bethel-luz|Genesis 28:19|Place names|intermediate|What earlier name does Genesis give for the place Jacob named Bethel?|Luz;Laish;Jebus;Kiriath-arba|Genesis identifies the former name as Luz. Laish, Jebus and Kiriath-arba are other biblical place names, not the earlier name given here.

dan-laish|Judges 18:29|Place names|intermediate|What was the city called before the Danites renamed it Dan?|Laish;Luz;Jebus;Debir|Judges explicitly names the city's earlier name as Laish; the alternatives are different settlements.

jerusalem-jebus|Judges 19:10|Place names|intermediate|Which older name is explicitly identified with Jerusalem in Judges 19?|Jebus;Luz;Laish;Kiriath-sepher|The narrator identifies Jebus as Jerusalem. The other names refer to different places.

hebron-name|Joshua 14:15|Place names|advanced|What former name of Hebron does Joshua 14 identify?|Kiriath-arba;Kiriath-jearim;Kiriath-sepher;Kiriathaim|The text calls Hebron's earlier name Kiriath-arba and associates Arba with the Anakim; the similar-looking alternatives name different places.

ebed-rescue|Jeremiah 38:7-13|Obscure people|advanced|Which court official obtained permission to rescue Jeremiah and supplied rags to cushion the ropes?|Ebed-melech;Shephatiah;Gedaliah son of Pashhur;Jucal|Ebed-melech appealed to the king and directed the rescue. The other officials belong to the group opposing Jeremiah, not to this rescue.

hilkiah-find|2 Kings 22:8-10|Priesthood|intermediate|Who reported finding the Book of the Law in the temple during Josiah's reign?|Hilkiah the high priest;Shaphan the scribe;Ahikam son of Shaphan;Asaiah the king's servant|Hilkiah found the book and gave it to Shaphan, who read it and reported to the king. Discoverer and reader are different roles.

shaphan-read|2 Kings 22:8-11|Obscure people|advanced|Who read the newly discovered Book of the Law before King Josiah?|Shaphan;Hilkiah;Ahikam;Achbor|Shaphan read the book before the king. Hilkiah discovered it; the surrounding narrative names other officials without assigning them this reading.

amaziah-amos|Amos 7:10-14|Prophets|advanced|Who told Amos to flee to Judah and stop prophesying at Bethel?|Amaziah the priest;Jeroboam the king;Uzziah the king;Hosea the prophet|Amaziah, priest of Bethel, addressed Amos in these terms. Jeroboam was the recipient of Amaziah's report, not the speaker of the command to flee.

amos-occupation|Amos 7:14-15|Prophets|advanced|What two occupations did Amos mention when replying to Amaziah?|Herdsman and dresser of sycamore trees;Fisherman and boat builder;Scribe and keeper of the treasury;Potter and worker in bronze|Amos described his work with herds and sycamore trees before recounting his call. The paired alternatives are occupations, but not his stated pair.

stephen-amos|Acts 7:42-43;Amos 5:25-27|Scriptural connections|mastery|Which prophet supplies the passage about Moloch's tabernacle quoted in Stephen's speech?|Amos;Hosea;Isaiah;Ezekiel|The quotation corresponds to Amos 5. Stephen's use and the wording of the earlier passage need to be distinguished from other prophets' warnings about idolatry.

hosea-egypt|Matthew 2:15;Hosea 11:1|Scriptural connections|mastery|Matthew applies a statement about calling a son out of Egypt to Jesus. In Hosea's original context, who is called the son?|Israel;Judah's king Ahaz;The prophet's son Jezreel;The priest Joshua|Hosea begins by naming Israel as the child whom God loved. Matthew applies the language to Jesus; the question asks about the original context.

rahab-line|Matthew 1:5-6|Genealogy|mastery|In the sequence Rahab, Boaz, Obed, Jesse, David recorded in Matthew, how many parent-to-child links separate Rahab from David?|Four;Two;Three;Five|The recorded sequence has four links: Rahab to Boaz, Boaz to Obed, Obed to Jesse, Jesse to David. This counts the written genealogy without asserting independently dated biological gaps.

athaliah-rescuer|2 Chronicles 22:11-12|Genealogy|advanced|Who hid the infant Joash and is identified as Jehoiada's wife and King Jehoram's daughter?|Jehoshabeath;Athaliah;Jezebel;Zibiah|Jehoshabeath, also called Jehosheba in Kings, hid Joash. Athaliah was the threat, and Zibiah was his mother, not Jehoiada's wife.

naaman-river|2 Kings 5:10-14|Geography|beginner|In which river did Naaman wash seven times as Elisha's message instructed?|Jordan;Abanah;Pharpar;Kishon|Naaman initially contrasted the Jordan with Abanah and Pharpar, the rivers of Damascus, but finally washed in the Jordan.

dothan-servant|2 Kings 6:13-17|Geography|advanced|Where was Elisha when his servant's eyes were opened to see horses and chariots of fire?|Dothan;Carmel;Gilgal;Samaria|The surrounding army came to Dothan. Carmel belongs to Elijah's well-known contest, and the other places do not identify this scene.

anoint-jehu|2 Kings 9:1-6|Prophets|advanced|Who instructed a member of the sons of the prophets to go to Ramoth-gilead and anoint Jehu?|Elisha;Elijah;Micaiah;Ahijah|Elisha commissioned the messenger. The messenger performed the anointing; Elisha's role was to send him with instructions.

joel-pentecost|Acts 2:16-21;Joel 2:28-32|Scriptural connections|intermediate|Whose prophecy did Peter explicitly cite to explain the outpouring of the Spirit at Pentecost?|Joel;Amos;Micah;Haggai|Peter introduces the quotation by naming Joel. The other prophets are not identified as its source in this speech.

herod-james|Acts 12:1-4|Same-name identities|advanced|Which James did Herod kill with the sword before imprisoning Peter?|James the brother of John;James the son of Alphaeus;James the Lord's brother;John the son of Zebedee|Acts specifies James as John's brother. The identifying relationship prevents confusion with the other people named James.

peter-rhoda|Acts 12:12-16|Obscure people|intermediate|Who recognised Peter's voice at the gate but ran to announce him before opening it?|Rhoda;Mary the mother of John Mark;Sapphira;Tabitha|Rhoda came to answer the door, recognised Peter's voice, and left the gate unopened in her joy. Mary owned the house where the group was praying.

paul-antioch|Acts 13:13-14|Geography|advanced|After leaving Perga in Pamphylia, which Antioch did Paul and his companions reach?|Antioch in Pisidia;Antioch in Syria;Iconium;Lystra|The passage specifies Antioch of Pisidia. The sending community's Antioch is a different city; Iconium and Lystra are later stops.

lydia-origin|Acts 16:14|Geography|intermediate|From which city was Lydia, the seller of purple whom Paul met at Philippi?|Thyatira;Philippi;Troas;Ephesus|Lydia was from Thyatira although the meeting took place at Philippi. Origin and encounter location are different facts.

sergius-office|Acts 13:6-7|Offices and roles|advanced|What office does Acts assign to Sergius Paulus when Paul meets him in Cyprus?|Proconsul;Tetrarch;Centurion;High priest|Acts identifies him as the proconsul. A tetrarch, centurion and high priest held different kinds of authority.

gallio-achaia|Acts 18:12-16|Offices and roles|advanced|Over which province was Gallio proconsul when Paul's opponents brought him to judgment?|Achaia;Asia;Syria;Cyprus|Gallio was proconsul of Achaia. The hearing took place at Corinth, so a city and a province must not be confused.

felix-successor|Acts 24:27|Kings and succession|intermediate|Who succeeded Felix as governor while Paul remained imprisoned?|Porcius Festus;Pontius Pilate;Sergius Paulus;Gallio|Acts says Porcius Festus succeeded Felix after two years; Felix left Paul bound.

paul-centurion|Acts 27:1-3|Obscure people|advanced|Which centurion of the Augustan band was entrusted with Paul for the journey to Italy?|Julius;Cornelius;Claudius Lysias;Sergius Paulus|Acts names Julius as the centurion. Cornelius was another centurion, Claudius Lysias a military commander, and Sergius Paulus a proconsul.

malta-chief|Acts 28:7-8|Obscure people|advanced|Whose father was healed by Paul after the shipwreck, on an estate where the travellers were welcomed?|Publius;Julius;Aristarchus;Mnason|Publius, the chief man of the island, received the party. It was his father who was ill; the other men have different roles in Paul's journeys.

tert-scribe|Romans 16:22|Obscure people|advanced|Who inserts a greeting identifying himself as the person who wrote down the letter to the Romans?|Tertius;Quartus;Gaius;Erastus|Tertius says that he wrote the letter and greets the readers. This distinguishes the scribe from Paul, the author, and from the other people sending greetings.

phoebe-church|Romans 16:1-2|Geography|advanced|With which church does Paul associate Phoebe when commending her to the Romans?|Cenchreae;Corinth;Philippi;Ephesus|Paul calls Phoebe a servant of the church at Cenchreae. The nearby city of Corinth is a plausible alternative but is not the named congregation.

chloe-report|1 Corinthians 1:11|Obscure people|intermediate|Whose household informed Paul about quarrels among the Corinthians?|Chloe's;Stephanas's;Crispus's;Gaius's|Paul explicitly attributes the report to Chloe's people. Other Corinthian households are mentioned nearby, but not as the source of this report.

epaphras-prayer|Colossians 4:12-13|Early church|advanced|Who does Paul describe as striving in prayer for the Colossians and caring for those in Laodicea and Hierapolis?|Epaphras;Epaphroditus;Tychicus;Aristarchus|Epaphras is named in this description. Epaphroditus is a different coworker with a similar name; Tychicus and Aristarchus have other roles in the letter.

carpus-cloak|2 Timothy 4:13|Obscure people|advanced|With whom had Paul left the cloak at Troas that he asked Timothy to bring?|Carpus;Crescens;Tychicus;Onesiphorus|Paul specifies Carpus at Troas. The other coworkers appear in the letter, but are not named as the person holding the cloak.

demas-place|2 Timothy 4:10|Geography|advanced|To which destination did Demas go after deserting Paul, according to 2 Timothy?|Thessalonica;Dalmatia;Ephesus;Troas|Demas went to Thessalonica. Dalmatia is associated with Titus in the same verse; Ephesus and Troas concern different people and instructions.

titus-winter|Titus 3:12|Geography|advanced|Where did Paul say he had decided to spend the winter when asking Titus to join him?|Nicopolis;Crete;Corinth;Troas|Paul asked Titus to come to Nicopolis. Crete was Titus's assigned field, not the winter meeting place named here.

zenas-lawyer|Titus 3:13|Offices and roles|advanced|Which person is called a lawyer in Paul's instruction to Titus about supplying travellers?|Zenas;Artemas;Tychicus;Apollos|Zenas is called the lawyer; Apollos is his travelling companion in the instruction, and Artemas and Tychicus appear in the preceding verse.

onesimus-return|Philemon 1:10-16|Early church|intermediate|For whom does Paul appeal as his child, asking that he be received beyond the status of a servant as a beloved brother?|Onesimus;Archippus;Epaphras;Demas|The appeal names Onesimus. The other coworkers are mentioned in the letter but are not the person at the centre of this request.

philemon-address|Philemon 1:1-2|Early church|advanced|Who is called a fellow-soldier in the opening address of Philemon?|Archippus;Onesimus;Epaphras;Aristarchus|The opening calls Archippus a fellow-soldier. This wording does not identify him with Onesimus or the companions named in the closing greetings.

melchizedek-tithe|Hebrews 7:1-4;Genesis 14:18-20|Scriptural connections|advanced|Who received a tenth from Abraham and is called king of Salem and priest of God Most High?|Melchizedek;Aaron;Eleazar;Zadok|Both the Genesis scene and Hebrews identify Melchizedek. The other men belong to the later Israelite priestly line.

hebrews-tribe|Hebrews 7:13-14|Priesthood|intermediate|Which tribe does Hebrews say the Lord descended from, in contrasting his priesthood with the altar-serving tribe?|Judah;Levi;Benjamin;Ephraim|Hebrews explicitly names Judah and notes that Moses spoke nothing about priests in connection with that tribe.

james-elijah|James 5:17-18|Scriptural connections|intermediate|Which prophet does James use as an example of a person like us whose prayers concerned the withholding and return of rain?|Elijah;Elisha;Isaiah;Jeremiah|James names Elijah and recounts the rain-related prayers. Elisha's other miracles do not make him the figure named here.

james-rahab|James 2:25|Scriptural connections|intermediate|Which woman does James cite for receiving messengers and sending them out by another way?|Rahab;Ruth;Deborah;Jael|James explicitly names Rahab. The question asks about the stated example, not a general comparison of the women's faith.

silvanus-letter|1 Peter 5:12|Early church|advanced|Through whom does the writer of 1 Peter say he has written briefly, calling him a faithful brother?|Silvanus;Mark;Timothy;Titus|Silvanus is named as the intermediary in verse 12. Mark sends a greeting in the next verse but is not assigned the same role.

noah-preacher|2 Peter 2:5|Scriptural connections|intermediate|Whom does 2 Peter call a preacher of righteousness in its account of the ancient world's judgment?|Noah;Lot;Enoch;Abraham|The passage calls Noah a preacher of righteousness. Lot appears next in a different judgment example.

cain-example|1 John 3:11-12|Scriptural connections|intermediate|Which man does 1 John name as an example of hatred toward his brother?|Cain;Esau;Joseph;Aaron|The letter names Cain and his brother. The other men had brothers but are not the man used as this example.

elect-lady|2 John 1:1|Textual nuance|intermediate|How does 2 John address its recipient without giving her a personal name?|The elect lady and her children;The widow of Zarephath and her son;Lydia and her household;Priscilla and her church|The address is to the elect lady and her children. The text does not supply a name or settle whether the address is personal or symbolic.

diotrephes|3 John 1:9-10|Early church|advanced|Who is criticised in 3 John for loving preeminence and refusing to receive the brethren?|Diotrephes;Demetrius;Gaius;Tertius|Diotrephes is criticised for these actions. Gaius is the addressee and Demetrius receives a good testimony, so those roles should not be reversed.

demetrius|3 John 1:12|Early church|intermediate|Who receives a good testimony from all and from the truth itself in 3 John?|Demetrius;Diotrephes;Gaius;Demas|Verse 12 names Demetrius. Diotrephes is criticised earlier; the similar name Demas belongs to other letters.

jude-body|Jude 1:9|Textual nuance|advanced|According to Jude, whose body was the subject of Michael's dispute with the devil?|Moses';Elijah's;Enoch's;Abraham's|Jude names Moses' body. The verse does not provide a detailed burial narrative, and the other named figures must not be substituted.

jude-triad|Jude 1:11|Scriptural connections|advanced|Which three figures occur together in Jude's warning about a way, an error for hire, and a rebellion?|Cain, Balaam and Korah;Abel, Balak and Aaron;Cain, Balak and Moses;Esau, Balaam and Aaron|Jude names Cain, Balaam and Korah in that order. The alternatives swap figures associated with the same narratives but not with this triad.

patmos|Revelation 1:9|Geography|beginner|On which island does John say he was because of God's word and Jesus' testimony?|Patmos;Cyprus;Crete;Malta|John identifies the island as Patmos. The other islands appear elsewhere in New Testament journeys.

laodicea|Revelation 3:14-16|Early church|intermediate|Which church is addressed with the rebuke that it is neither cold nor hot?|Laodicea;Philadelphia;Smyrna;Pergamum|The address beginning in verse 14 names Laodicea; the other cities receive their own distinct messages.

antipas-witness|Revelation 2:12-13|Obscure people|advanced|Which faithful witness is named as having been killed where the church at Pergamum lived?|Antipas;Stephen;James;Silas|The message to Pergamum names Antipas. This witness should not be identified with Herod Antipas merely because the written name is shared.

creation-lights|Genesis 1:14-19|Primeval history|beginner|On which day in Genesis 1 are the lights appointed to distinguish days, seasons and years?|Fourth;First;Second;Third|The lights are described in the fourth day's account. Light itself appears earlier, so the question specifically asks about the lights appointed for these functions.

noah-bird|Genesis 8:8-12|Primeval history|beginner|Which bird returned to Noah with a freshly plucked olive leaf?|Dove;Raven;Eagle;Sparrow|The dove returned with the leaf. Noah had also sent a raven, making it a nearby narrative alternative rather than the correct bird.

terah-move|Genesis 11:31|Patriarchs|intermediate|Where did Terah's household settle after setting out from Ur toward Canaan?|Haran;Shechem;Bethel;Hebron|The family came to Haran and lived there. The other places belong to later patriarchal journeys, not Terah's stop in this verse.

sarah-burial|Genesis 23:17-20|Geography|intermediate|Which burial place did Abraham acquire from Ephron for Sarah?|The cave of Machpelah;The cave of Adullam;The cave at Makkedah;The tomb of Rachel|The purchased field and cave were at Machpelah, before Mamre. The other burial or cave sites are not the property bought from Ephron.

rebekah-brother|Genesis 24:29|Genealogy|beginner|Who is named as Rebekah's brother when he runs out to meet Abraham's servant?|Laban;Bethuel;Nahor;Haran|Genesis identifies Laban as her brother. Bethuel is her father, while Nahor and Haran occupy different places in the family.

joseph-cup|Genesis 44:1-2,12|Patriarchs|intermediate|In whose sack was Joseph's silver cup found after the brothers left Egypt?|Benjamin's;Judah's;Reuben's;Simeon's|Joseph instructed the steward to place it in the youngest brother's sack; the search found it with Benjamin. The discovery was arranged, not evidence that he stole it.

ephraim-hand|Genesis 48:13-14,17-19|Genealogy|advanced|Which of Joseph's sons received Jacob's right hand despite being the younger?|Ephraim;Manasseh;Reuben;Simeon|Jacob knowingly placed his right hand on Ephraim. Manasseh was Joseph's firstborn; Reuben and Simeon are mentioned in Jacob's preceding comparison but were not Joseph's sons.

joseph-bones|Joshua 24:32;Genesis 50:25|Scriptural connections|advanced|Where were Joseph's bones buried after the Israelites brought them from Egypt?|Shechem;Hebron;Bethel;Shiloh|Joshua records the burial at Shechem. Joseph's request in Genesis explains why his bones were brought from Egypt.

midwives|Exodus 1:15-17|Obscure people|intermediate|Which two midwives are named as refusing the king of Egypt's order to kill Hebrew boys?|Shiphrah and Puah;Miriam and Zipporah;Leah and Rachel;Hannah and Peninnah|The passage names Shiphrah and Puah and says they feared God rather than carrying out the king's command.

moses-basket|Exodus 2:3|Exodus and wilderness|beginner|What was used to waterproof the basket in which Moses' mother placed him?|Bitumen and pitch;Oil and salt;Wax and incense;Clay and lime|The basket of bulrushes was daubed with bitumen and pitch. The question concerns the coating rather than the material of the basket itself.

moses-sons|Exodus 18:3-4|Genealogy|intermediate|Which son of Moses had a name explained by Moses' deliverance from Pharaoh's sword?|Eliezer;Gershom;Eleazar;Ithamar|Eliezer's name is explained by God's help and deliverance. Gershom's explanation concerns being a sojourner; Eleazar and Ithamar were Aaron's sons.

marah|Exodus 15:23|Geography|intermediate|Where could the Israelites not drink the water because it was bitter?|Marah;Elim;Rephidim;Sinai|The narrative explicitly connects Marah with the bitter water. Elim is the following stop with springs and palms.

elim-springs|Exodus 15:27|Exodus and wilderness|advanced|What combination does Exodus record at Elim?|Twelve springs and seventy palms;Seven springs and twelve palms;Twelve springs and forty palms;Seventy springs and twelve palms|Exodus records twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees at Elim. The alternatives alter the two stated quantities.
